ORTHOGRAPHIC VERTICAL OVERHEAD PLAN VIEW. Camera directly above, looking straight down onto the object from above. Rectangular edges run horizontally and vertically on the canvas. Show no vertical outside faces.

Create an ORIGINAL game sprite for an empty military heavy-drop airdrop platform, the flat metal pallet a vehicle is strapped to before it is dropped by parachute. Images 1 and 2 are our approved pieces from the same game, seen from directly above: match their outline weight, shading, steel colours and finish only. Do NOT copy their shapes.

Tall portrait canvas. The platform is a long rectangle with its long sides running from the TOP edge to the BOTTOM edge, filling the canvas with a small even margin, on a plain pure white background.

The platform seen from above: a flat bare-aluminium deck made of several panels laid across it, with thin dark seams between the panels; a raised steel side rail along the whole of the left edge and the whole of the right edge, with small round tie-down rings spaced evenly along both rails; slightly rounded corners; and on the deck, four evenly spaced flat rectangular stacks of yellow-tan cardboard honeycomb crush pads, their tops showing a simple honeycomb of large hexagon cells.

Style: a sprite for the game RimWorld: a thick near-black outline around every shape, soft flat cel shading with two or three tones per material, muted aluminium grey and tan colours, a few small clean details, no texture noise. Not a photograph, not a 3D render, not pixel art.

No text, letters, numbers, stencils, logos, people, vehicles, cargo, straps across the deck, parachutes or wheels. No ground beyond the object, no shadow outside it, no perspective, no tilt.
